condition: suspected acute lithium neurotoxicity presenting with abrupt severe coarse bilateral hand tremor in an older adult on daily lithium
level_rationale: Abrupt-onset severe coarse shaking in the hands today in a 70-year-old man taking daily lithium capsules is a classic hallmark of acute lithium toxicity in an older adult requiring immediate hospital stat serum lithium and renal electrolyte measurement, electrocardiography, intravenous isotonic saline resuscitation, and evaluation for extracorporeal clearance, whereas a mild brief shudder in the hands when holding a teacup over the past week on daily lithium warrants a routine outpatient prescribing-doctor review.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult-son carer lexical register swap (-reg) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + Rule A first-choice same-hand-tremor mild lithium side-effect outpatient control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (70-year-old father, daily oral lithium capsules, and abrupt severe coarse shaking in his hands today) with finite clause coordination ('and receives' / 'and takes'), a 1-word span difference (15 vs 14 words), 11 shared trailing tokens, and zero diagnosis labels ('bipolar' omitted from prompt texts). Isolating the acute lithium neurotoxicity sign in f3 prevents stranding vomiting or confusion, and under Rule A first choice and Rule D changes only hand-tremor severity to verbatim patient wording ('a little bit of a shudder in the hands', PMID 35475375) shifting right care from emergency hospital evaluation (level 4) to routine outpatient doctor review (level 2).
